01

Setting specification

Task

Find an approximately stationary point of the reduced objective $\Phi$, obtained by maximizing the payoff over the second block. Return the primal point $\widehat x$.

$$ \min_x\Phi(x),\quad\Phi(x)=\max_y f(x,y). $$

Admissible model

$f:\mathbb{R}^{d_x}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_y}\to\mathbb{R}$, with both blocks unconstrained and Euclidean norms throughout. The joint gradient satisfies $\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le \beta\|z-w\|_2$.

The condition $f\in C^2$ holds, and the full joint Hessian satisfies $\|\nabla^2f(z)-\nabla^2f(w)\|_{\rm op}\le\rho\|z-w\|_2$.

For every $x$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is uniformly $\mu_y$-strongly concave. Thus $y^\star(x)=\arg\max_y f(x,y)$ is unique and $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^\star(x))$ is differentiable. Neither $f(\cdot,y)$ nor $\Phi$ is assumed convex.

Assume $\inf_x\Phi(x)>-\infty$, with an initial point satisfying $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$.

The public initial point additionally satisfies $\|y_0-y^\star(x_0)\|_2\le R_y$. The condition number is $\kappa=\beta/\mu_y$.

Oracle interface

Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $\Delta$, $R_y$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $\mu_y$, $\rho$, together with the stated initial point and feasible geometry. The analytic representation of the hidden function, operator, or matrix is not revealed.

$$ z\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}\longmapsto(f(z),\nabla f(z),\nabla^2f(z)). $$

One exact call returns the complete joint Hessian, function value, and joint gradient.

Inner optimizers, reduced gradients, and reduced Hessians are not supplied directly. Linear algebra on returned data does not reveal new information about hidden functions.

Output

Return $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^{d_x}$.

The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

Accuracy is the Euclidean norm of the gradient of the reduced objective at the returned primal point. For each admissible instance, the norm must be at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$.

$$ \|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2 $$

The reduced gradient is $\nabla\Phi(x)=\nabla_xf(x,y^\star(x))$. Second-order stationarity is not the target.

Resource accounting

A bundled value, gradient, and full-Hessian response costs one $N_{\mathrm{bundle}}$ call. Derivative costs are not split further.

Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

A single algorithm is chosen from the public input and must satisfy the guarantee for every fixed admissible instance.

$$ \Pr\!\left(\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon\right)\ge\frac23. $$

Probability is over private algorithmic randomness only. The unknown instance is fixed before interaction.

Budget convention
fixed worst-case query cap
02

Notation and parameters

$A_1$

The primal progress scale obtained using first-order smoothness alone.

Domain
Positive real number

$A_1=\Delta\beta/\varepsilon^2$

$A_2$

Scale of the leading second-order high-accuracy term

Domain
Positive real number

$A_2=\Delta\sqrt\rho\,\kappa^{3/4}\varepsilon^{-3/2}=A_1\sqrt r$

$C_0$

Universal sufficient constant in the nontrivial accuracy regime; no numerical value is specified.

Domain
Positive constant without an assigned numerical value
$\Delta$

A public bound on the initial reduced-objective value above its infimum. Attainment of the infimum is not required.

Domain
Positive real number

$\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$

$I_0$

Initialization-call upper bound for the first regularized saddle problem; the relations below specify its verified polynomial scale and hidden logarithms

Domain
Nonnegative resource upper-bound function

$I_0\le\widetilde O(\mathcal S_{\rm init})$

$M_{\mathrm{main}}$

The scale determining whether the leading term dominates initialization.

Domain
Positive real number

$M_{\mathrm{main}}=A_1\Psi_\kappa(r)$

$\Psi_\kappa(r)$

Dimensionless multiplier in the three-branch full-Hessian rate.

Domain
Positive real number

$\Psi_\kappa(r)=\begin{cases}r^{1/2},&0<r\le1,\\ r^{2/7},&1\le r\le\kappa^{7/4},\\ \kappa^{1/2},&r\ge\kappa^{7/4}.\end{cases}$

$R_y$

Distance bound from the initial dual point to the unique best response at the same initial primal point

Domain
A nonnegative real.

$\|y_0-y^\star(x_0)\|_2\le R_y$

$R_{y,0}^{\mathrm{prox}}$

A bound on dual distance from the initial point to the first regularized saddle point.

Domain
Positive real number

$R_{y,0}^{\mathrm{prox}}=R_y+\kappa\sqrt{\Delta/\beta}$

$\mathcal S_{\mathrm{init}}$

The explicit power-law scale of the initialization upper bound, excluding unexpanded logarithms.

Domain
Positive real number

$\mathcal S_{\mathrm{init}}=1+\min\{\sqrt\kappa,(\rho R_{y,0}^{\mathrm{prox}}/\mu_y)^{2/7}\}$

$\beta$

Euclidean Lipschitz upper bound for the population payoff's complete joint gradient.

Domain
Positive real number

$\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le\beta\|z-w\|_2$

$d$

The joint Euclidean dimension is $d=d_x+d_y$. Within its stated window, the lower bound may choose finite block dimensions.

Domain
Integer at least $2$
$\varepsilon$

Euclidean norm tolerance for the true reduced gradient; the mean-square contract targets its square $\varepsilon^2$.

Domain
Positive real number
$\kappa$

Ratio of the population smoothness upper bound, or mean-square average smoothness for finite sums, to the dual strong-concavity lower bound

Domain
$\kappa\ge1$

$\kappa=\beta/\mu_y$

$\mu_y$

A uniform strong-convexity lower bound for −f(x,·) at every fixed x; equivalently, the dual strong-concavity modulus of f.

Domain
$0<\mu_y\le\beta$

$f(x,v)\le f(x,y)+\langle\nabla_yf(x,y),v-y\rangle-\frac{\mu_y}{2}\|v-y\|_2^2$

$r$

Dimensionless ratio separating the main complexity regimes

Domain
Positive real number

$r=\rho\kappa^{3/2}\varepsilon/\beta^2$

$\rho$

Lipschitz upper bound for the complete joint Hessian in spectral norm.

Domain
Positive real number

$\|\nabla^2f(z)-\nabla^2f(w)\|_{\rm op}\le\rho\|z-w\|_2$

$\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$

Euclidean norm and inner product; the product-space norm is the square root of the sum of the squared block norms.

Domain
The specified finite-dimensional real vector space.

$\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$

$d_x,d_y$

Positive integer primal and dual block dimensions; joint dimension $d=d_x+d_y$

Domain
Positive integer
$f$

Unknown real-valued payoff, with primal and dual input blocks.

Domain
$f:(x,y)\mapsto f(x,y)\in\mathbb R$
$x,y,z$

Primal variable, dual variable, and joint point

Domain
$x\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ y\in\mathbb R^{d_y},\ z=(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}$

$z=(x,y)$

$\nabla f,\nabla_x f,\nabla_y f$

Complete joint gradient and its two blocks

Domain
$\nabla_x f\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ \nabla_y f\in\mathbb R^{d_y}$

$\nabla f=(\nabla_x f,\nabla_y f)$

$\nabla^2 f$

Complete joint Hessian, including both diagonal and both mixed blocks

Domain
The matrix $(d_x+d_y)\times(d_x+d_y)$ is real symmetric.
$\Phi$

Reduced objective after global dual maximization; neither its value nor gradient is an additional free interface

Domain
Real-valued function on the primal-variable space

$\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in \mathbb R^{d_y}}f(x,y)$

$y^\star(x)$

The unique global dual maximizer at fixed primal x.

Domain
$y^\star(x)\in\mathbb R^{d_y}$

$y^\star(x)=\arg\max_{y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}}f(x,y)$

$\|\cdot\|_{\rm op}$

Matrix or multilinear tensor norm induced by the Euclidean norm

Domain
Matrix and derivative tensors used in this profile

$$ \|T\|_{\rm op}=\sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_j\|_2\le1}\|T[u_1,\ldots,u_j]\|_2 $$

$x_0,y_0$

The public initial primal and dual variables.

Domain
The respective feasible domains. Both equal zero when the origins are explicitly fixed.
$\widehat x$

The point or variable blocks ultimately returned by the algorithm, corresponding to the hatted variables in the error formula.

Domain
A feasible primal point in $\mathbb R^{d_x}$.
$\mathbb E,\Pr$

Expectation and probability over the explicitly allowed algorithm and sample randomness, with the hidden instance fixed.

Domain
Operations on the corresponding probability space
$N_{\rm bundle}$

Number of bundled function-value, complete joint-gradient, and complete-Hessian calls

Domain
Nonnegative integer count; expected work is its expectation.
$N$

A uniform cap on principal information calls for every admissible instance and execution path.

Domain
Nonnegative integer
$N^\star$

The infimum principal query budget among algorithms satisfying every stated instancewise output guarantee.

Domain
Nonnegative extended real value; by convention, positive infinity if no successful algorithm or no uniform finite budget exists
$\mathcal A,I$

An algorithm selected from public inputs and an admissible hidden instance fixed before interaction

Domain
The specified algorithm and model classes.
$\omega$

A complete realization of algorithmic and sample randomness.

Domain
Corresponding sample space
$O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde O$

Asymptotic upper and lower bounds, constant-factor matching, and upper bounds hiding the stated logarithmic factors, within the corresponding regions.

Domain
Nonnegative complexity function; subscript p permits additional dependence only on fixed p
$\mathfrak A_\varepsilon$

Algorithms using the allowed interfaces, algorithm restrictions, and output domain, and satisfying the displayed complete error guarantee for every fixed admissible instance

Domain
The algorithm class is defined at fixed public parameters and target tolerance $\varepsilon$.
03

Complexity bracket

Each bracket applies to the stated view, success guarantee, resource and parameter region. Status summarizes the documented comparisons.

Compared quantities and resource definitions

Q1 · target accuracy cost

\[N^\star(\varepsilon)=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_\varepsilon}\sup_I \sup_\omega N_{\rm bundle}(\mathcal A,I,\omega)\]
Scope
Take the worst case over admissible finite-dimensional instances. Theorems with dimension conditions apply only within those windows and do not establish fixed-dimensional saturation rates.
Optimization direction
minimize

One call is charged for the full response specified by the interface. The algorithm class obeys the declared randomization, adaptivity, and output rules and must satisfy the complete error guarantee on every fixed admissible instance. The call cap is uniform over instances and execution paths.
